sections.h2: Where is North Charleston, SC, and which counties does it cover?
sections.html:
North Charleston spreads across three counties, Berkeley, Charleston and Dorchester, in the Lowcountry north of the city of Charleston. The Ashley River forms much of its southwest edge and the Cooper River its southeast edge, and it borders Charleston, Hanahan, Goose Creek, Ladson and Summerville.

These numbers come from the city's Wikipedia entry. The three-county split is the first thing a North Charleston seller should sort out, because the county decides who assesses the property, who bills the tax and where the deed is recorded.

sections.h2: How did the Navy and Boeing shape North Charleston?
sections.html:
North Charleston grew around the Charleston Naval Shipyard, established in 1901, and the Naval Base that operated from 1902 to 1996. Voters approved incorporation in an April 27, 1971 referendum, and the city was incorporated on June 12, 1972. In 2010 the Air Force Base and the Naval Weapons Station merged into Joint Base Charleston.

Employers named in the city entry include:

  • Boeing, which chose North Charleston in October 2009 for a 787 Dreamliner assembly line.
  • Kapstone, with about 1,100 workers at its kraft paper mills.
  • InterContinental Hotels Group, with more than 400 call center workers.
  • iQor, with 360 workers, and Mercedes-Benz vans, with 200.

The Hugh K. Leatherman Terminal, a 280-acre container facility, opened its first phase in April 2021. Those worker counts come from the Wikipedia article and may be out of date, so treat them as a rough guide.

sections.h2: What is the weather like, and what flood questions come up?
sections.html:
North Charleston's weather record, taken at Charleston International Airport, shows average annual precipitation of 51.03 inches and about 2,809 hours of sunshine. The mean July high is 91.1 degrees, the mean January low is 37.5 degrees, and snowfall averages just 0.5 inches a year. Those are 1981 to 2010 normals.

The bigger risk is water. Hugo in September 1989 caused more than $2.8 billion in damage across the Lowcountry. Charleston County's flood flyer advises homeowners to learn their flood zone, flood depth and flood history, because standard homeowners insurance generally does not cover flood damage.

  • A flood policy typically starts 30 days after purchase.
  • A house in a Special Flood Hazard Area with a federally backed mortgage must carry flood insurance.
  • Premiums depend partly on elevation, and an agent may request an elevation certificate.

If a prior owner raised the house or elevated its equipment, that paperwork helps a buyer's insurer, so gather it before you list.

sections.h2: Which schools and transport links do North Charleston buyers ask about?
sections.html:
North Charleston is served by two school districts, Charleston County School District and Dorchester School District Two, and the right one depends on the address. High schools named in the city entry are North Charleston High, R.B. Stall High, Academic Magnet High, Military Magnet Academy and Fort Dorchester High, which is in Dorchester District Two. Higher education includes Charleston Southern University, Trident Technical College and ECPI University.

Getting around, according to the same entry:

  • Charleston International Airport serves more than 2.9 million passengers a year.
  • Amtrak, Norfolk Southern and CSX provide passenger and freight rail.
  • CARTA runs the city bus system.
  • A planned intermodal center would combine a train station, long-haul bus service and CARTA at one site.

The entry does not name specific interstates, so check a map for exits near your house. Ask a local agent how commute to the airport, port or base affects your street.

sections.h2: Which North Charleston neighborhoods have the oldest housing?
sections.html:
Park Circle was one of the first areas planned in 1912, with industrial, commercial and residential sections. When the city incorporated, it took in Russelldale, Ferndale, Morningside, Liberty Park, Palmetto Heights, Singing Pines, Dewey Hill, Liberty Homes and John C. Calhoun Homes.

The city's parks include Riverfront Park and Northwoods Park, as well as Park Circle itself. Older neighborhoods can have aging wiring, plumbing and roofs, and repair costs are something a financed buyer's inspector will raise. A cash sale does not require you to make those repairs first.

The city's own pages list a Code Enforcement department, Business Licenses, Zoning with an online map, Building Inspections and a Certificate of Occupancy page.

sections.h2: How do North Charleston property taxes and assessments work?
sections.html:
The county that holds your parcel assesses it, so the part of North Charleston in Charleston County uses the county's rules, and parcels in Berkeley or Dorchester follow those counties.

In Charleston County, the county FAQ puts a primary residence at a 4 percent assessment ratio and other real estate at 6 percent. Tax equals assessed value times millage, and one mill is one thousandth of a dollar. Owners who live in the house apply for the 4 percent legal residence status, and the county recommends filing early in the year.

State law makes taxes payable between September 30 and January 15, with penalties of 3, 7 and 5 percent that start after that date, as set out in Chapter 45. Reassessment notices went out in August 2025 with an appeal deadline of November 18, 2025, per a notice from a nearby town. Properties sold or transferred are an exception to the 15 percent cap.

The county Auditor handles real estate questions at (843) 958-4234 or RealProperty@CharlestonCounty.org.

sections.h2: What happens at closing, and what about inherited or landlord-owned houses?
sections.html:
Charleston County parcels are recorded at the Register of Deeds, 101 Meeting Street, Suite 200, Charleston, open 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. on weekdays, phone (843) 958-4800. The state's deed fee is $1.85 per $500 of value, and estate distribution deeds are excluded under Chapter 24.

For disclosure, Title 27, Chapter 50 requires a written statement from an owner unless the sale is exempt. Transfers by a fiduciary administering an estate, guardianship or trust are exempt, which is useful if you are an executor selling a parent's home. The law also allows as-is deals.

The city entry reports that North Charleston had the highest eviction filing and judgment rate among U.S. cities of 100,000 or more as of 2016. Landlords with problem tenants may therefore find a cash sale of an occupied house worth comparing with listing it.

Cash Home Buyers reviews North Charleston houses in their current condition and states any offer in writing. Whether we make one depends on the house.

faqs.q: What county is North Charleston in?
faqs.a: North Charleston lies in Berkeley, Charleston and Dorchester counties. Which one applies to your house decides your tax bill, assessor and Register of Deeds.

faqs.q: What are the main employers in North Charleston?
faqs.a: The city entry names Boeing's 787 line, Kapstone's paper mills, InterContinental Hotels Group, iQor and Mercedes-Benz vans. The Leatherman Terminal container port and Joint Base Charleston are also major anchors.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed for a Charleston County house in North Charleston?
faqs.a: Use the Charleston County Register of Deeds at 101 Meeting Street, Suite 200, Charleston. Parcels in Berkeley or Dorchester go to those counties.

faqs.q: Do I have to disclose problems if I inherited the house?
faqs.a: A fiduciary administering an estate is exempt from the written disclosure statement under South Carolina law. Heirs who sell in their own names may not be, so confirm with an attorney.

faqs.q: Is flood insurance required to sell a North Charleston house?
faqs.a: No, but a buyer with a federally backed mortgage on a house in a Special Flood Hazard Area must carry it. Policies usually take 30 days to start.

faqs.q: When are North Charleston property taxes due?
faqs.a: State law sets the window from September 30 to January 15. Penalties of 3, 7 and 5 percent follow after that date.
